t: You're on City Road, a road running through central London. At its north-western end is the Angel, where it continues on from Pentonville Road. That road is the modern name for part of London's first bypass, the New Road from Paddington to Islington, built in 1756. City Road followed in 1761, carrying the route on to the City of London. John Henry Ingram, an English biographer and editor with a special interest in Edgar Allan Poe, was born here.
